ignatius-sancho.name: Charles Ignatius Sancho
ignatius-sancho.summary: Composer, writer, abolitionist; widely thought to be the first Black Briton to vote in a parliamentary election (1774, 1780).

olaudah-equiano.name: Olaudah Equiano
olaudah-equiano.summary: Abolitionist and author of 'The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano' (1789), a foundational text of the British anti-slavery movement.

mary-seacole.name: Mary Seacole
mary-seacole.summary: Jamaican-British nurse and businesswoman who set up the British Hotel during the Crimean War to care for sick and wounded soldiers.

samuel-coleridge-taylor.name: Samuel Coleridge-Taylor
samuel-coleridge-taylor.summary: Composer of 'Hiawatha's Wedding Feast' (1898). Born in Holborn, raised in Croydon; one of the most successful English composers of his generation.

harold-moody.name: Harold Moody
harold-moody.summary: Jamaican-born physician who founded the League of Coloured Peoples (1931) in London, the leading civil-rights organisation for Black Britons before the war.

claudia-jones.name: Claudia Jones
claudia-jones.summary: Trinidad-born journalist and activist who, after deportation from the US, founded the West Indian Gazette (1958) and originated what became the Notting Hill Carnival.

francis-barber.name: Francis Barber
francis-barber.summary: Jamaican-born manservant, heir, and confidant of Samuel Johnson; central figure in 18th-century literary London.

kwame-kwei-armah.name: Kwame Kwei-Armah
kwame-kwei-armah.summary: British playwright, director and actor. Author of 'Elmina's Kitchen' (2003), 'Fix Up' and 'Statement of Regret'; artistic director of the Young Vic 2018–2023.

yvonne-brewster.name: Yvonne Brewster
yvonne-brewster.summary: Jamaican-British director; co-founder and longtime artistic director of Talawa Theatre Company (founded 1986), Britain's oldest Black-led theatre company.

una-marson.name: Una Marson
una-marson.summary: Jamaican poet, journalist, BBC broadcaster — the BBC's first Black woman programme-maker; producer of 'Caribbean Voices'.

mary-prince.name: Mary Prince
mary-prince.summary: Bermudian-born abolitionist whose 1831 testimony, dictated at the Anti-Slavery Society's London office, was the first slave narrative by a Black woman published in Britain.

ottobah-cugoano.name: Quobna Ottobah Cugoano
ottobah-cugoano.summary: Ghanaian-born abolitionist and author of 'Thoughts and Sentiments on the Evil of Slavery' (1787); co-founder with Equiano of the Sons of Africa, Britain's first known Black political organisation.
